clue.text: Room to stretch your legs

parts.note: reads as a request for legroom, but means a chamber where a victim is stretched on the rack

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a roomy seat on a plane; the stretching is done by a rack, an old instrument of torture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon with a rack was where prisoners' limbs were cruelly pulled.

clue.text: They are plain sounding champagne's

parts.note: a champaign, which sounds like the wine, is an old word for open level country, so these are such flat expanses

explanation.surface: Some sparkling wines are described as plain-tasting.
explanation.walkthrough: Champaign (open flat country) is said like the wine Champagne; the clue calls the answer plains that sound like champagnes. It is a cryptic definition, not a true homophone of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Treeless Arctic plains are open level country, once called champaigns.

clue.text: Pelt of domestic animals

parts.note: looks like the fur of pets, but pelt is the verb for heavy rain falling, in an idiom naming two household pets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' seems to be an animal's hide; here it is the verb, to pour down hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a downpour so heavy it seems pets are falling from the sky.

clue.text: Au fait at university working

parts.note: being up means being in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
on means operating or working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Someone at university is fully informed about the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well informed on a subject is to be knowledgeable and up to date.

clue.text: Inferior pigeon fancier

definitions.note: a noun here: an inferior follower or imitator

indicators.note: read as more fanciful, so the letters of the word pigeon are given a fancier arrangement

explanation.surface: A pigeon fancier who is not much good at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancier' looks like a person who breeds pigeons; it is the anagram signal on PIGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a second-rate imitator of a great artist or thinker.

clue.text: Ran into the Hague with such fulmination

indicators.note: one word is put into another, so the word ran goes inside the city name

parts.note: The Hague is the Dutch seat of government
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ran into The Hague ranting furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hague is the Dutch city where the international courts sit; 'into' is the container signal, splitting the city's name after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulmination is a loud, angry tirade, a long ranting speech.

clue.text: Given drawing qualities of a certain attraction

definitions.text: Given drawing qualities of a certain attraction

parts.words: Given drawing qualities of a certain attraction
parts.note: suggests an artist's talent or charm, but means made able to pull iron, a particular kind of attraction

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching and 'attraction' charm; both are about magnetic pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of iron treated so that it pulls other metal toward it has been made a magnet.

clue.text: Current cover for one out for the rest of the night

definitions.text: Current cover for one out for the rest of the night

parts.words: Current cover for one out for the rest of the night
parts.note: sounds like insurance for a reveller, but current is electricity and the cover is bedding for someone asleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is electrical current; 'out' means asleep, resting through the night under a heated bed covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated bed covering runs on mains power to warm a sleeper.

clue.text: Question worker about sidelong glance

definitions.note: the answer is an adverb, with a sidelong glance; the clue gives the noun phrase

parts.note: to question is to ask
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone questions an employee about a shifty look.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means obliquely, looking sideways out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Robinia wildly produced here

indicators.note: growing wildly suggests the letters of the plant name are run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A robinia tree grows wild in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points to the place the anagram names: ROBINIA rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Kenya is the place where, in the surface, the tree grows.

clue.text: Sets off, from the start, such vessels

indicators.note: read as taking away from the start, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: something that sets off an event triggers it

explanation.surface: Ships setting off from the starting line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the start' removes the first letter T from TRIGGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigger is a ship described by its rig, as in a square-rigger.

clue.text: He's a jerk

parts.note: reads as an insult about a man, but takes a man's name that is also a word for a sudden wrench or twist

explanation.walkthrough: A rick is a sprain from a sudden jerk, and Rick is a man's name, hence 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp wrench of a joint is a sprain, and the same word is a boy's name.

clue.text: Petitions a movement for a Christmas plant

indicators.note: movement of the letters means the words petitions and a are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest movement petitions for a festive plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like a campaign behind the petitions; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-leaved Mexican shrub is a favourite seasonal decoration in December.

clue.text: Suave Edna o'brien became disorganised

indicators.note: letters that became disorganised are jumbled, so the two name words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The novelist Edna O'Brien lost track of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Edna O'Brien is an Irish novelist; her name is anagram fodder. This spelling with -AIRE is an older variant.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth, charming and urbane in manner is the meaning of both words.

clue.text: Sofa is hard to support

parts.note: set means hardened, as concrete sets
a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: A sofa that is too hard to give proper support.
explanation.definitionFit: A long upholstered seat for two or more is a couch.

clue.text: Dog I record is a boxer

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
taken as written
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a dog is a boxer breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' looks like the dog breed, but it means a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prizefighter who fights with fists is the classical name for a boxer.

clue.text: It can turn on Ada wearing this boa

indicators.note: Ada wearing something means it is put on, so she surrounds the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the words can and on take a turn, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snake may coil itself round a woman named Ada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges CAN into NAC; 'wearing' has Ada dress herself in it. 'It' and 'this' just point the surface at the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge South American constrictor is a kind of boa.

clue.text: Fire spitting muskets put round in termagants

indicators.note: the round letter is put in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a termagant is a fierce woman, colloquially a dragon
a round letter is O

explanation.surface: Fire-breathing beasts and weapons among quarrelsome women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places O inside DRAGONS. A dragoon was originally a short musket, said to breathe fire like a dragon.
explanation.definitionFit: The early carbine carried by mounted soldiers spat flame, which gave such troops their name.

clue.text: Back rod over such amount

indicators.note: turned over means the word rod is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: A rod laid over someone's back for a certain amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal signal, giving DOR; 'Back' is the anatomical sense, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the term means the upper or rear surface of the body.

clue.text: Recall it is not about a subscriber

indicators.note: not means the following word is left out of the longer one

parts.note: to recall is to remember
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A subscriber who fails to recall something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes RE (about) from REMEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pays dues to join a club belongs to it as one of its number.

clue.text: Jackets for smoking in, in joints

definitions.meaning: short double-breasted coats worn by sailors
cannabis cigarettes, the things for smoking

explanation.surface: Smoking jackets worn in pubs or dives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for smoking in' seems to describe smoking jackets but belongs to the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sailor's thick coat and a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Division of Yorkshire may yield to the whip

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings, North, East and West
a crop is a harvest or yield

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire district gives way to party discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: A riding is one of the historic divisions of Yorkshire, an English county. 'the whip' sounds parliamentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stick with a loop used by horse riders is a type of whip.

clue.text: Initially bitter beer causes misery

indicators.note: initially tells us to take just the first letter of the word bitter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A pint of bitter turns out to cause woe.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale beer, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for woe, evil or suffering, as in baleful.

clue.text: The shock of Barnet

parts.note: sounds like an upset in a London borough, but Barnet is rhyming slang for what grows on the head, and a shock is a thick mass of it

explanation.walkthrough: Barnet Fair is Cockney rhyming slang for the stuff on your head; Barnet is also a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a bushy mop of the stuff growing on a person's scalp.

clue.text: To enter up ian is of impracticable perfection

indicators.note: one word enters another, so to goes inside up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Ian is entered in some impossible ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' is the container signal; the lower-case 'ian' is a man's name disguised in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes an ideal society too flawless to be realised, after More's imaginary island.

clue.text: Hamper to find at the hovel with the French

parts.note: a shack is a crude hut, a hovel
le is the masculine French for the

explanation.surface: Searching a French hut for a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket; it is the verb, to restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict someone's movement is to fetter or chain them.

clue.text: Rio atheists rot from joint complaint

indicators.note: the answer is made from these words, so their letters are rearranged to form it

explanation.surface: Unbelievers in Brazil decay from arthritis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the answer is made from RIO ATHEISTS ROT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A degenerative disease of the cartilage that causes stiffness and pain in the knees, hips and hands.
